Cast iron. The heavier the better. No teflon. I'll repeat: no teflon.

The point is that to stirfry, you want the son of a b*tch to get super-hot before adding oil and ingredients, so that adding the cold ingredients does not lower the heat of the pan significantly. And you want to be able to toss the contents with a good big sturdy metal spoon or spatula or what do you call it in English. (slotted spoon?), so no teflon please. Also, if you get the iron really hot, it does not need an anti-stick coating, it will be its own anti-stick coating. To be able to really dig and toss, the pan needs to be as heavy as you can get it. Also, size matters - the bigger, the easier to toss bigger meals. However, you can't throw it in the dishwasher, but that's only a minor annoyance to me.

If you get a light, teflon coated pan you'll mainly cook the ingredients due to the lower heat, and you won't be able to use sturdy metal spoons to stir.

I have owned a cast iron wok for over 30 years now, and it is the best thing in my kitchen. Go for it, you won't be sorry.
